purpose: Explain the replicated combination of lower rooted armed membership with higher recruitment hazard and foothold strength by measuring actual recruited population flow and the recruitment-state terms that were not present in the original replication output.

design.reason_for_reuse: This is a mechanistic decomposition of already-known replication outcomes, not an independent confirmation.

primary_decomposition: Treatment-minus-baseline cumulative recruited mass at day 240.
Treatment-minus-baseline recruited mass accumulated from day 240 to day 360.
Excess recruited mass through day 240 divided by direct underground disruption mass through day 240.
Treatment-minus-baseline eligible recruitment mass and recruitment hazard at day 240 and day 360.
secondary_decomposition: Treatment-minus-baseline social exposure, grievance, fear, political access, foothold strength, and insurgent social capital at day 240 and day 360.
Compare the five known day-360 rebound seeds against the eleven suppressed seeds descriptively.
Correlate excess recruitment-flow ratios with day-360 rooted-membership effects as exploratory diagnostics only.
interpretation_rules: Because endpoint outcomes on this seed block are already known, no relationship discovered here is confirmatory.
If U produces positive excess recruited mass, that directly supports compensatory replacement flow rather than merely a higher instantaneous hazard.
If rebound seeds have greater post-intervention excess recruitment than suppressed seeds, promote that predictor only through a future fresh-seed contract.
Do not attribute the effect to disrupted_sympathy_retention; that parameter has a separately documented semantic mismatch and is unchanged here.
